title: skill-spec/v0
description: Vocabulary a thin, tool-calling skill's semantics render from: a closed verb surface, three guardrail lists, and a per-verb capsule-emission declaration. A skill validated against this schema is data a generator renders into host-specific shapes (a Claude Code SKILL.md, a Codex AGENTS.md, ...); it is never itself a place to write reasoning, prose justification, or anything the generator does not render.

name.description: Lowercase, hyphenated skill identifier; becomes the rendered SKILL.md frontmatter `name`.

description.description: One-line summary of what the skill does and when to use it; becomes the rendered SKILL.md frontmatter `description`.

may.description: What the skill is authorized to do. Human-authored guardrail wording (see the item's HUMANS-WRITE-FIRST gate); a generator never invents or edits these strings, only renders them verbatim.

must_never.description: What the skill is forbidden from doing, rendered verbatim alongside `may`.

approval_points.description: Moments where the skill must stop and get an explicit human go-ahead before continuing. May be empty when a skill has none, but the key itself is always present.

verbs.description: The skill's entire action surface. A verb entry documents one command the underlying tool actually implements today; a spec must never carry a verb the tool does not implement, and a tool verb the spec omits is simply not available to the skill yet.

name.description: The command as the host agent types it, e.g. `contract validate` or `cll list`.

args.description: One entry per accepted invocation shape, in the tool's own flag syntax. Empty when the verb takes no arguments.

when.description: The single condition under which the skill calls this verb. A directive, not a design rationale.

emits.description: The capsule kind (or kinds) this verb's invocation results in, named well enough that a reader can find it in a CLL: e.g. a payload shape like `discover-scan/v1`, or a note that the verb's own result IS the capsule with no wrapper.

emission_mode.description: How `emits` actually happens: `self-sealing` — the verb has its own `--seal-output` and needs nothing further; `primary-action` — the verb's entire job is to create or chain a capsule (e.g. `publish`, `cll append`), so running it already satisfies the invariant; `skill-wraps` — the verb only reads or checks something, so the skill must itself call the base `seal` command over the verb's JSON result to leave a record that the check happened.
